A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, replaced and removed material to be distinguished.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction comparisons, module ablations, template-mismatch experiments, simulated grasping results and physical robot experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original reconstruction results, quantitative ablations, the TAX3D comparison and physical grasping results, including the reported 77% success rate.

M1.justification: The conditional flow-matching method, geometry-guided feature propagation and alignment, view-adaptive aggregation, inference rule and training losses remain unchanged. Removing detailed grasp-transfer documentation does not establish a changed procedure. The DINOv3 training clarification is consistent with its previously stated pretrained initialization.

E1.justification: v3 removes the cross-category and cross-super-category template-mismatch scenarios from v1 A.7 and the evaluation on Nano-Banana-generated target images in Figure 11. These remove distinct input conditions and an image domain. The main ShapeNetv2/OakInk coverage and real-world grasping task remain.

E2.justification: The grasping comparison against DFC, ConGen, UGG, Tink and cmtDiff in v1 Table 3 disappears. The separate Phidias-3D comparison in the template-assignment experiment also disappears. Main reconstruction comparators remain; TAX3D is retained, with its table renumbered from Table 5 to Table 3.

E3.justification: v3 removes the reported no-retraining evaluation across three template-selection regimes and its same-subcategory Phidias-3D control. It also omits the grasping benchmark protocol specifying 10 targets per category, five template grasps and success/penetration/coverage metrics. Main reconstruction splits, rendering settings, metrics and training budgets remain unchanged; no rerun or changed setting is established for retained experiments.

E4.justification: The template-mismatch robustness study in v1 A.7, Table 4 and Figure 8 is removed, as is the qualitative module-ablation analysis in Figure 7; quantitative ablations remain in Table 2. The occluded-mug-handle failure case is replaced by an extreme-viewpoint chair case concerning unequal reconstructed leg lengths in v3 A.5 and Figure 7.

E5.justification: v1 A.4 reports averaging over 10 randomized-pose simulation trials and five physical trials per object. v3 omits both repetition disclosures. This is reduced statistical reporting, not evidence that fewer trials were performed; neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, Figure 4 and the relocated TAX3D comparison retain their results. v3 removes the grasping comparison, including Our-MV's 76.92% simulated success rate, and the template-mismatch results, including overall CD values of 2.56, 7.36 and 12.42 across the three regimes. Category-specific physical success rates and supplementary qualitative results disappear, while the overall physical rate remains 77%. The failure example is replaced.

T1.justification: Deleting v1 A.4.1 removes the mathematical specification of the contact/fingertip grasp-synthesis objective, Equation 18, and its constituent energy definitions. The core flow-matching, feature-modeling and geometric-loss equations, Equations 1–17, remain unchanged. No new proof or derivation is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and concluding contribution summary retain the same claims about geometry-guided deformation, viewpoint robustness, unseen-category generalization and dexterous manipulation. Reduced supporting evidence is not accompanied by a narrowing of these headline claims.

C2.justification: v3 removes the explicit template-mismatch failure boundary and replaces the hidden-handle explanation with perspective-induced ambiguity in global shape proportions. Future work shifts from multi-view target inputs toward language-informed representations, although language priors were already proposed in v1. Section 3.1.1 also replaces the assertion of preserved theoretical guarantees with the narrower statement that single-step inference retains the continuous-flow training objective.

D1.justification: v3 removes substantial grasping reproducibility information: contact/fingertip optimization details, SAM3 preprocessing, robot-hand configuration, execution instructions and physical success criteria. Core model hyperparameters, hardware and training time remain. A.3 adds 'except DINOv3' to the from-scratch training description, clarifying the already-described pretrained encoder.

R1.justification: v3 removes the CoS3D citation and appendix-linked references including SAM3, Isaac Gym, Gemini, Grasp as You Say and the Shadow Hand reference. The main related-work organization and positioning remain substantially unchanged. Bibliographic updates to retained works do not introduce new research comparisons.

P1.justification: Most main-text wording and section organization are retained. Changes include rewriting the limitations/future-work passages, revising the single-step explanation, shortening and renumbering the appendix, updating cross-references and publication information, and correcting an acknowledgment typo.

P2.justification: The appendix loses the grasping and template-assignment tables and four supplementary figures covering ablations, template mismatch and additional reconstructions/grasps. The mug failure illustration is replaced by a chair illustration. The retained TAX3D table and figure are relocated and renumbered from Table 5/Figure 9 to Table 3/Figure 8. Main-text displays remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 usefully tempers the single-step guarantee assertion and clarifies DINOv3 initialization. However, it removes the quantitative grasp-baseline comparison and essential measurement, implementation and trial details while retaining the competitive-grasp and 77% success claims. It also removes the template-mismatch stress test and its explicit applicability boundary. The replacement chair failure example does not compensate for these substantial losses in evidential support, reproducibility and limitations disclosure, despite unchanged core reconstruction results.
